core_obligations: Show the formula is invariant under replacing s_i by u s_i for a unit u of B_i: the first expression gains -ord_{B_i}(g_i) div(u|_{Z_i}) by well-definedness of divisors of meromorphic functions while the second gains div(partial(u^{-1}, g_i)) by bilinearity of the tame symbol, and these agree by normalisation (proof lines 4761-4775).

Reduce to comparing one coefficient at a time: fix an irreducible closed Z of delta-dimension n - 2 with generic point xi, set A = O_{X,xi} (a two-dimensional Noetherian local domain), choose trivialising generators sigma and tau of L_xi and N_xi, shrink X so that the Z_i are finite in number and Z is contained in each of them, and use the invariance of the previous paragraph together with its analogue for t_i to reduce to a_i = b_i = 1 (proof lines 4777-4800).

Conclude the reduced case: with a_i = b_i = 1 the first expression vanishes by the choice of the trivialising sections, and the coefficient of Z in the second expression becomes the sum over the height one primes q_i of ord_{A/q_i}(partial_{B_i}(f, g)); this sum is zero by the vanishing lemma, which finishes the proof (proof lines 4802-4816).
proof_roadmap: Check invariance under unit rescalings of the two trivialising sections (proof lines 4761-4775).
Reduce to one coefficient and then, by choosing trivialisations, to the case where the local sections are the trivialising generators (proof lines 4777-4800).
Evaluate the remaining sum of orders and invoke the vanishing lemma (proof lines 4802-4815).
difficulty_reason: The key formula equates two cycles on X: one built from orders of the local sections f_i and g_i multiplied by the divisors of the trivialising sections of two invertible sheaves, the other from the divisors of the tame symbols partial_{B_i}(f_i, g_i) (statement lines 4745-4758, tag 0AYC). The proof establishes invariance of the identity under rescaling the local trivialising sections, which mixes well-definedness of divisors with the bilinearity and normalisation property of the tame symbol, and then reduces to comparing a single coefficient by localising at a two-dimensional Noetherian local domain and choosing trivialisations so that the first expression collapses. The reduction is the substance of the argument, so the claim is H2.
